option_relations.rationale: The patient's symptoms of episodic sharp, electric-shock–like pain in the V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve, triggered by jaw movement, are consistent with the clinical presentation of trigeminal neuralgia.
Classical trigeminal neuralgia is a subtype of trigeminal neuralgia, characterized by the same symptoms and clinical presentation.
Secondary trigeminal neuralgia is a subtype of trigeminal neuralgia, but the patient's symptoms do not clearly indicate a secondary cause.
The patient's symptoms do not match the clinical presentation of cluster headache.
The patient's symptoms do not match the clinical presentation of persistent idiopathic facial pain.
The patient's symptoms do not match the clinical presentation of painful post.
The patient's symptoms do not match the clinical presentation of herpes zoster.
The patient's symptoms do not match the clinical presentation of glossopharyngeal neuralgia and dental pathology.
